newsitem.title: USA: U.S. military sends assessment team to Congo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. military sends assessment team to Congo.

text.p: A U.S. military assessment team was flown to troubled Brazzaville in the Congo on Tuesday to prepare for any requested evacuation of Americans from the troubled African capital, the Defence Department said.

Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon said the team of about a dozen communications specialists, security troops and planners arrived in the Brazzaville on Tuesday afternoon on a C-130 military transport from Germany.
He stressed, however, that no request had been made by the U.S. Embassy to evacuate Americans.

Bacon told reporters there were believed to be some 60 Americans in Brazzaville including about 15 workers at the embassy, which remained open despite reports of heavy gunfire among warring factions in the city.
"The situation there is quite chaotic now," he said, but added that the gunfire did not appear to be targeting Americans or other foreigners.

Bacon said some Americans would be taken out of Brazzaville on the C-130 in which the assessment team arrived and that any further evacuation would probably be handled by U.S. military cargo planes from Europe.
The United States on Monday called for a ceasefire between rival factions battling in the Congo capital and said it believed presidential elections could still be held on schedule on July 27.
Bacon praised French troops in the city for helping provide security and evacuating some Americans earlier.

"We are relying now on the French for security in the area and also to help escort some of our people to the airport or out of the country," he said. "The French have been performing very well and have been extremely helpful."
